competition: Bangladesh Mathematical Olympiad, National Round (Higher Secondary)

problems.problem: Find all non-negative integer solutions $(x,y,z)$ of the equation $$x!+2^y=z!$$ (Here $x!=x\cdot(x-1)!$ and $0!=1$; for example, $5!=5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1=120$.)

Let $\{a_1, a_2,\ldots,a_n\}$ be a set of $n$ real numbers whose sum equals $S$. It is known that each number in the set is less than $\frac{S}{n-1}$. Prove that for any three numbers $a_i$, $a_j$ and $a_k$ of the set, $a_i+a_j>a_k$.

For any positive integer $n$, define $f(n)$ to be the smallest positive integer that does not divide $n$; for example, $f(1)=2$ and $f(6)=4$. Prove that for any positive integer $n$, either $f(f(n))$ or $f(f(f(n)))$ is equal to $2$.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezium inscribed in a circle $\omega$, with $AB\parallel CD$. Let $P$ be a point on the circle $\omega$, and let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be the orthocenters of triangles $PAD$ and $PBC$ respectively. Prove that the length of $H_1H_2$ remains constant as $P$ varies on the circle.
Consider an integrable function $f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that $af(a)+bf(b)=0$ whenever $ab=1$. Find the value of the integral $$\int_{0}^{\infty} f(x) \,dx.$$

We are given $n$ intervals $[l_1,r_1],[l_2,r_2],\ldots, [l_n,r_n]$ on the number line, which can be divided into two sets such that no two intervals in the same set overlap. Prove that there are at most $n-1$ pairs of overlapping intervals.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and $\omega$ its circumcircle. The perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$ intersects $BC$ at $D$ and $\omega$ again at $K$. The circle through $A$ and $D$ tangent to $BC$ at $D$ intersects $\omega$ again at $E$. The line $AE$ intersects $BC$ at $T$, and $TK$ intersects $\omega$ again at $S$. Let $SD$ intersect $\omega$ again at $X$. Prove that $X$ is the reflection of $A$ in the perpendicular bisector of $BC$.

Joy has an $n \times n$ board. At every step, he colours a cell of the board; he cannot colour any cell more than once. He also counts points while colouring: at first he has $0$ points, and at every step, after colouring a cell $c$, he takes the largest possible set $S$ of cells forming a "$+$" sign whose cells are all coloured and whose centre is $c$, and he gets $|S|$ points. After colouring the whole $n \times n$ board, what is the maximum possible number of points he can have?

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $D$ be the point on side $BC$ such that $AD$ bisects the angle $\angle BAC$. A line $l$ is tangent to the circumcircles of triangles $ADB$ and $ADC$ at the points $K$ and $L$, respectively. Let $M$, $N$ and $P$ be the midpoints of $BD$, $DC$ and $KL$, respectively. Prove that $l$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $MNP$.

Consider all polynomials of degree $2023$ $$P(x)=x^{2023}+a_1x^{2022}+a_2x^{2021}+\cdots+a_{2022}x+a_{2023}$$ with real coefficients such that $P(0)+P(1)=0$ and $P$ has $2023$ real roots $r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{2023}$ (not necessarily distinct) with $0\leq r_i\leq1$ for all $i$. What is the maximum value of $r_1 r_2 \cdots r_{2023}$?
Find all prime numbers $p$ and $q$ such that $$p^3-3^q=10.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a square. Points $E$ and $F$ lie on the sides $AB$ and $BC$, respectively, such that $BE = BF$. The line through $B$ perpendicular to $CE$ intersects $CE$ and $AD$ at the points $G$ and $H$, respectively. The lines $FH$ and $CE$ intersect at the point $P$, and the lines $GF$ and $CD$ intersect at the point $Q$. Prove that the line $DP$ is perpendicular to the line $BQ$.

Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2024}$ be a permutation of $1, 2, \ldots, 2024$. Find the minimum possible value of $$\sum_{i=1} ^{2023} \left[(a_i+a_{i+1})\left(\frac{1}{a_i}+\frac{1}{a_{i+1}}\right)+\frac{1}{a_ia_{i+1}}\right].$$

Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$ and $P$ a point such that $PI$ is perpendicular to $BC$ and $PA$ is parallel to $BC$. The line parallel to $BC$ which is tangent to the incircle of triangle $ABC$ (other than $BC$) intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at the points $Q$ and $R$ respectively. Prove that $\angle BPQ = \angle CPR$.
Find all polynomials $P(x)$ for which there exists a sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ of real numbers such that $$a_m + a_n = P(mn)$$ for all positive integers $m$ and $n$.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $$f\left(\left\lceil \frac{f(m)}{n} \right\rceil\right)=\left\lceil \frac{m}{f(n)} \right\rceil$$ for all $m,n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Let $k$ be a positive integer. Show that there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $\frac{n^n-1}{n-1}$ has at least $k$ distinct prime divisors.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $M$ the midpoint of the side $BC$. The perpendicular bisector of $BC$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at the points $K$ and $L$, where $K$ and $A$ lie on opposite sides of $BC$. A circle passing through $L$ and $M$ intersects $AK$ at the points $P$ and $Q$, with $P$ on the segment $AQ$. The line $LQ$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $KMQ$ again at $R$. Prove that $BPCR$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

Juty and Azgor play the following game on a $(2n+1) \times (2n+1)$ board, with Juty moving first. Initially all cells are white. On Juty's turn, she colours a white cell green, and on Azgor's turn, he colours a white cell red. The game ends when all cells of the board are coloured. Juty wins if all the green cells are connected, i.e. any two green cells are joined by a chain of green cells in which consecutive cells are neighbours (two cells are neighbours if they share at least one corner); otherwise Azgor wins. Determine which player has a winning strategy.

One day a room contained several inhabitants of an island where only truth-tellers and liars live. Three of them made the following statements:
• "There are no more than three of us here. We are all liars."
• "There are no more than four of us here. Not all of us are liars."
• "There are five of us here. At least three of us are liars."
How many people are in the room, and how many of them are liars?

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with circumcenter $O$ and orthocenter $H$. Let $D, E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A, B$ and $C$ to the opposite sides, respectively, and let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ in the line $EF$. Prove that $HOA'D$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

Two players play on a $100 \times 100$ grid. Initially the whole board is black. On his move, $A$ selects a $4 \times 4$ subgrid and colours it white; on his move, $B$ selects a $3 \times 3$ subgrid and colours it black. $A$ wants to make the whole board white. Can he do it?
Find all prime numbers $p, q$ such that $$p(p+1)(p^2+1) = q^2(q^2+q+1) + 2025.$$

Let the incircle of triangle $ABC$, with center $I$, touch the sides $BC, CA$ and $AB$ at the points $D, E$ and $F$ respectively. Let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to the line $AD$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $DE$. If $N$ is the intersection point of $PM$ and $AC$, prove that $DN \parallel EF$.

Yamin and Tamim play a game with subsets of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, where $n \geq 3$.
• Tamim starts the game with the empty set.
• On Yamin's turn, he adds a proper non-empty subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ to his collection $F$ of blocked sets.
• On Tamim's turn, he adds to his set, or removes from it, one positive integer at most $n$; however, he can never make a move after which his set is one of the blocked sets in $F$.
Tamim wins if he can make his set equal to $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$; Yamin wins if he can prevent this. Yamin goes first and they alternate moves. Does Tamim have a winning strategy?
Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(xf(y)-y) + f(xy-x) + f(x+y) = 2xy$$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

In triangle $ABC$, $DB$ and $DC$ are tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Let $B'$ be the reflection of $B$ in the line $AC$, and similarly let $C'$ be the reflection of $C$ in the line $AB$. If the line $BC$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $DB'C'$ at $E$ and $F$, prove that $AE = AF$.
If $\frac{b}{a}=5$ and $\frac{c}{b}=7$, find the value of $\frac{a+b}{b+c}$.
Let $f$ be a continuous function satisfying $f(1+x)=f(1-x)$ for every real $x$. It is given that the equation $f(x)=0$ has exactly $2026$ distinct roots. Find the sum of all the roots.
$ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral, and $F$ is the midpoint of the arc $AB$ not containing $C$ or $D$. Let $P = CF \cap BD$ and $Q = DF \cap AC$. Prove that $PQ \parallel AB$.

Let $S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}$. Mr. Teham chooses a pair of elements of $S$ and writes down the greater number of the pair; for example, if he chooses $\{6, 7\}$ he writes $7$. Find the sum of all the numbers he has written after choosing every possible pair exactly once.

Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. Points $E$ and $F$ are two distinct points on the arc $AB$ of its circumcircle not containing $C$. Let $D = CE \cap AB$ and $G = CF \cap AB$.
(1) Prove that $CE \cdot DG = k \cdot EF \cdot CG$ for some real number $k$ not depending on the points $E$ and $F$.
(2) Find the value of $k$.
Prove that for every positive integer $n$ $$I_n = \int_{0}^{1} x^{n}\sqrt{1-x}\,dx = \frac{2^{2n+2}\,n!\,(n+1)!}{(2n+3)!}.$$
Find all positive integers $n$ of the form $n = p^k$, where $p$ is a prime number and $k$ is a positive integer, such that $$n = x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x - 1$$ for some integer $x$.
Find all triples $(k, m, n)$, where $k$ is a prime number and $m, n$ are non-negative integers, such that $$k^m - n^3 - 1 = 26.$$

Let $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{1013}\}$ and $\{b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{1013}\}$ be two disjoint subsets of $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2026\}$ such that $|a_i - b_i| \equiv 1 \pmod{5}$ for all $1\le i\le 1013$, and let $$S = \sum_{i=1}^{1013} |a_i - b_i|.$$
(1) Prove that $S \equiv 3 \pmod{5}$.
(2) Prove that $S \equiv 1 \pmod{2}$.
(3) Prove that the last decimal digit of $S$ is $3$.

There are $n$ people in a math camp. Each person has exactly $8$ acquaintances in the camp. If two people are acquainted with each other, then exactly $4$ other people are acquainted with both of them; if two people are not acquainted with each other, then exactly $2$ other people are acquainted with both of them. Find all possible values of $n$.
